text.p: Bankrupt Dutch aircraft pioneer Fokker NV took another step towards oblivion on Wednesday after potential saviour Malaysia said it did not expect a proposed rescue to go ahead.
The following is a chronology of the main events in the history of Fokker.
* 1912 -- Anthony Fokker begins building planes for German army, including fighters like the Fokker triplane favoured by the Red Baron in World War One.
* 1919 -- Fokker established as a commercial company.
* 1928 -- Fokker is world's biggest plane-maker, designing revolutionary aircraft like the Fokker IV which made aviation history with a coast-to-coast crossing of the U.S. in 1922.
* 1957 -- Fokker launches the famous F27 Fokker Friendship turboprop, still in service.
* 1969 -- Fokker enters cooperation pact with German aerospace manufacturer VFW, but the relationship is tense from the start.
* 1980 -- Fokker and VFW go their separate ways.
* 1981 -- Fokker and McDonnell Douglas of the U.S. decide to work together.
* 1983 -- Fokker launches plans to build the F50 and F100 jets at a development cost of 1.6 billion guilders.
* 1985/86 -- F50 and F100 make their debut flights.
* 1986 -- Fokker shares hit a high of 99.50 guilders on optimism about F50 and F100 programmes.
* 1987 -- Dutch state saves Fokker from threat of bankruptcy caused by spiralling development costs, taking 49 percent equity stake in company.
* 1990 -- Fokker recovers, posts profit of 83 million guilders.
* 1991 -- Fokker sets out to find new partner.
* 1993 -- Daimler-Benz AG's DASA unit agrees to pay 686 million guilders for a 51 percent stake in Fokker.
* 1994 -- Fokker announces first of a string of heavy losses and sacks 1,100 of its 13,000 workforce.
* JULY 1994 -- Dutch government and DASA pump one billion guilders of fresh capital into the company.
* AUGUST 1995 -- Fokker posts record first-half loss of 651 million guilders. Shares slump to 5.60 guilders.
* SEPTEMBER 1995 -- Two major shareholders, DASA and Dutch state, refuse Fokker request for another 2.3 billion guilders.
* JANUARY 1996
-- Daimler Benz cuts off financial support. Dutch state says it will explore other rescue options.
-- Canada's Bombardier surfaces as possible saviour.
-- Dutch state offers 255 million guilder credit line to keep Fokker alive while it looks for buyer.
* FEBRUARY 1996
-- Fokker in talks with five serious potential buyers (Samsung, British Aerospace, France's Aerospatiale, Taiwanese government and Bombardier)
-- Bombardier says it no longer interested.
* MARCH 1996 -- Fokker declares bankruptcy at three core units. Non-core businesses such as space systems, electronics and aircraft services live on, but need new partners.
* APRIL 1996 -- Fokker says Samsung no longer interested in bidding for company.
* JUNE 1996 -- Fokker remains in production after Dutch airline KLM orders seven 70-seat aircraft.
* JULY 1996 -- Dutch industrial systems group Stork buys Fokker Aviation, Fokker's parts, maintenance and special services unit.
* AUGUST 1996 -- Samsung re-emerges as possible buyer.
* SEPTEMBER 1996 -- Samsung begins due diligence procedures.
* OCTOBER 1996 -- Samsung hands Fokker business plan to Dutch Economics Ministry.
-- Administrators tell staff that rescue deadline is end-October.
* NOVEMBER 5, 1996 -- Dutch government expects decision on Samsung takeover "within days".
* NOVEMBER 13, 1996 -- Samsung invites South Korea's Daewoo and Hyundai to take part in Fokker rescue.

* NOVEMBER 28, 1996 -- Court-appointed administrators at Fokker said they had ended possible rescue talks with Samsung after Shorts, one of Fokker's suppliers, said it would no longer supply wings for Fokker aircraft.
* DECEMBER 20, 1996 -- Russian plane-maker Yakovlev, mooted as a possible buyer in August, says it still optimistic it can purchase Fokker.
* DECEMBER 31, 1996 -- South Korean government informs Dutch government that it is ruling out a takeover by the consortium led by Samsung Aerospace.
* JANUARY 28, 1997 -- Yakovlev says still interested.
* FEBRUARY 13, 1997 - Stork confirms it in negotiations with industrial group Begemann and a large Singapore finance company aimed at Fokker relaunch.
* FEBRUARY 19, 1997 - Malaysian government reported as latest in long line of potential Fokker saviours.
* MARCH 6, 1997 - Billionaire Saudi Prince al-Waleed bin Talal touted as possible Fokker white knight.
* MARCH 11, 1997 - Yakovlev says still trying to put together a Russian consortium to buy Fokker.
* MARCH 13, 1997 - Fokker administrators say they, Dutch state, Stork and Deleye Investment agree common approach to put to Malaysian government in fresh rescue bid.

* APRIL 7, 1997 - Stork says it no longer bound to memorandum of understanding on Fokker restart. Fokker almost completed building its last three aircraft and many of its remaining employees have left.
* APRIL 9, 1997 - Malaysia says does not expect a proposed rescue of Fokker to go ahead after Stork demands Malaysia put up money first before allowing a due diligence study of Fokker.
